To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cognitive constraints are a central factor in integrative systems biological model-building, 2) the cognitive complexity of modeling biological systems is handled by simulative mental modeling practices, 3) these modeling practices are constrained by the need for cognitive economy and 4) these constraints help us to understand the limited scope and success of current modeling in integrative systems biology.

(1) computational model-building in systems biology is a cognitive process that depends on simulative mental modeling; (2) simulative mental modeling is a form of cognitive modeling; (3) simulative mental models are a form of cognitive representation; (4) simulative mental representation is constrained by the computational model-building process and the computational modeling of systems biology; and (5) these constraints limit what is modeled and what is left unmodeled in systems biology.

(1) computational modeling is a human cognitive practice, (2) cognitive processes of simulative model-building play a central role in the practice of computational modeling in systems biology, and (3) cognitive constraints on model-building limit the scope of the representational choices available to systems biologists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the cognitive complexity of integrative systems biology modeling is managed.
the role of cognition in integrative systems modeling and the constraints that cognition puts on model-building.
the question how computational modeling and simulation in integrative systems biology is cognitively constrained.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the complexity of the systems biology modeling problems is not only handled computationally but that it is cognitively constrained.
computational modeling in integrative systems biology is not only a tool for solving biological problems but also a cognitive tool for solving modeling problems.
cognitive constraints are a necessary part of the story of how integrative systems biology works.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the computational modeling of biological systems in systems biology is constrained by the cognitive complexity of the problem of building models of biological systems.
integrative systems biology is a field of scientific inquiry that is both cognitive and computational in nature.
integrative computational systems biology is not a science of complexity in the way that some have suggested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of the biological systems that integrative systems biology aims to study and control is not only reflected in computational model complexity but also in cognitive complexity.
computational simulation and other computational tools do not simply solve problems in systems biology.
computational modeling in integrative systems is an essentially cognitive activity, one in which modelers must engage in simulative mental modeling in addition to computational modeling.
